Pinned FermionResearch/phonon-coreml 1.1.2, commit bf59e574639b060e30ee1a3f9c0e003fed5744c8.
Apache-2.0, upstream LICENSE and NOTICE retained.
uiui changes: library-only Swift package, host macOS 14 compatibility via macOS 15 availability on Transcriber; require local precompiled model, remove automatic compile/cache fallback. Model weights remain unchanged. The default empty-vocabulary path uses the original compiled decoder.

uiui runtime cancellation: Options.checkCancellation hook surrounds model predictions; one-worker/one-encoder profile uses a serial window loop with the same encoder, greedy decoder, rescue and timestamp stitch. This avoids queued speculative work and checks cancellation before subsequent windows/rescues. Native active requests are not preempted.

2026-10-24 compact vocabulary integration:
- Sources/PilotTDT, BiasPhrases.swift, and decoder-container validation come from the verified build/phonon-vocabulary-v3/cache-decoder candidate; ContextGate.hpp comes from its frozen sibling context directory. Local include paths and SwiftPM binary-target linkage replace research-directory paths. The original PhononTDT xcframework is unchanged. The C create wrapper now rejects a missing original-reference allocation rather than exposing an unusable handle.
- Compact int8/FP16 coefficient tables, immutable-history predictor caching, and at most four demand-driven GEMV jobs are unchanged. Inference never requests the optional dense test reference. Context configuration is fixed to budget 8, margin 8, mode 2, maxLoss 8, K 16, predictor cache enabled.
- Transcriber.configureVocabulary(_:) atomically replaces cloned decoder handles between sessions on the host's owner executor; the shared DecoderTables and existing Core ML models remain loaded. Up to 100 unique normalized terms are considered. Empty/unspellable lists use the original reference decoder. Native automaton overflow falls back for the entire pool; asset/clone failures propagate. Public initialization/options remain compatible.
- Vendor tests retain the candidate's meaningful compact numeric, context, cache, parser, and cancellation probes. New pool tests cover idempotence, shared tables, bounded input, whole-pool fallback and recovery. Tests using the official decoder locate it at the host repository's resources/Phonon/decoder.bin; no speech inference is required.
- Construction-only bias, suppression, word-start, and selective C setters contain allocation exceptions and quarantine the unpublished handle. A sticky C status distinguishes allocation failure from the existing zero-state capacity signal; Swift propagates allocation failure and preserves the prior pool. A model-free deterministic fault diagnostic exercises all four guarded paths. Nonallocating setters retain the frozen behavior.

2026-10-24 integrated execution optimization:
- WindowDecodeCache.swift retains bounded raw token/frame/duration output for exactly unchanged windows in the serial one-encoder/one-decoder path. Keys include exact Float32 input bits, window/function identity and the configuration/reset epoch. PCM and encoder features are not retained. Rescue and timestamp/text stitching still run with current context.
- At most 16 entries and 8,192 token triples are retained per cache state. Cache updates are transactional: failed/cancelled transcriptions do not publish them. Reset and vocabulary reconfiguration invalidate the cache. The library option defaults off; uiui enables the qualified serial profile.
- Unit tests cover exact-key invalidation, bounds, reset, cancellation and transaction publication. Integrated public/synthetic replay preserves all 312 final outputs and ordered live snapshots compared with the uncached compact decoder. See the host docs/compact-decoder-integration.md for qualification and resource measurements.

2026-10-24 round-one host allocation reduction:
- ArraySource windows now borrow PCM with an internal synchronous ArraySlice helper. File/custom AudioSource implementations retain their existing read contract. RMS scans use the same helper; their arithmetic, full-source recomputation and planner rules are unchanged.
- LogMel accepts borrowed slices, including nonzero-based long windows and rescue halves, with the same pre-emphasis, frame counts and whole-window normalization. This removes the source-to-window and window-to-mel PCM copies for array-backed decode misses; exact-window cache hits remove the source-to-window copy. No growing-window mel/features or new PCM cache is introduced.
- The qualified serial execution profile constructs only its fast decoder; the previously idle worker handle is omitted across initial creation and vocabulary replacement/fallback. Concurrent profiles retain distinct worker and fast handles. Model weights, decoder options, audio/context, rescue, revisions and transcript construction remain unchanged.
- Focused model-free tests cover borrowed storage, custom-source reads, bit-exact RMS/planner and mel parity, input replacement/shrink/growth, exact slice hashes and changed-bit invalidation, plus serial/concurrent decoder-pool construction and vocabulary fallback. The host's serialized validation passed all 67 vendor tests and completed the root suite with 461 tests, zero failures and one skip because the isolated pasteboard service was unavailable. Runtime replay and benchmarking remain pending; these notes do not assert a measured speedup.
- Float-format (decoder.bin v3) handles now support selective vocabulary bias. They have no compiled int8 reference, so the unbiased reference pass is a plain greedy decode over the same float weights (no trie bonus, not counted against the prediction budget); the existing rollback and commit rules then apply unchanged. int8 (v2) handles are byte-identical to before. `Transcriber.Options.selectiveVocabulary` (default true) exists for evaluation only.

2026-10-29 glued number spacing:
- GluedNumberSpacing.swift (+ generated GluedNumberWords.swift, 65,269 lowercase dictionary words of 3+ letters) is a faithful port of the digit-spacing rule from the ASR analysis (digsp.py): "at10" -> "at 10", "July2020" -> "July 2020", "5minutes" -> "5 minutes", "3pm" -> "3 pm"; identifiers (HbA1c, x1, 11th, 1990s, 3D, md5, ch1, fy26, 10mm, spo2) stay glued. Tokens touching URL/e-mail/path/code joiners are left alone. Idempotent; only ASCII letter/digit runs are examined.
- Applied once, to Transcript.text in finishTranscript, so the app (PhononModelPool transcribes `.text`) and phonon-eval share one path. Words and Segments keep raw decoder text. `Options.spaceGluedNumbers` (default true) turns it off for evaluation.
